title: Sturgeon and Others (Joined Cases C-402/07 and C-432/07), 19 November 2009
source: Sturgeon and Others (Joined Cases C-402/07 and C-432/07), 19 November 2009
excerpt: passengers whose flights are delayed may be treated, for the purposes of the application of the right to compensation, as passengers whose flights are cancelled and they may thus rely on the right to compensation laid down in Article 7 of the regulation where they suffer, on account of a flight delay, a loss of time equal to or in excess of three hours, that is, where they reach their final destination three hours or more after the arrival time originally scheduled by the air carrier.
summary: Passengers who reach their final destination three hours or more late can claim compensation as if the flight had been cancelled.
